Wording observation (not RED): `change_fee_fare_bands_2f62ad06` closes with "The fare that bands the change fee is measured from the fare collected on the ticket, which is every fare-collection and add-collect entry on its fare history." The source factor binds `chg_fare_collected` as the quantity the banding fare is measured from, and the convention (taxes and fees subtracted for an active agreement; coupon value flown subtracted otherwise) lives in its own method document. "Measured from" is used the same way across the corpus (`same_day_change_fare_bands_bcf911d2`: "measured from these two quantities"; `bag_charge_fare_bands_01da7c59`: "measured from the ticket's fares"), and the dedicated definition document is reachable by the exact defined term. No visible sentence equates the banding fare with the fare collected, so the visible materials do not entail a second formula. The sentence names only one of the convention's inputs, however. A solver who reads it as "equals" reaches GT's method-factor baseline (55.89 instead of 58.32). Recorded as a hazard of the rendering, not as a bijection or runtime failure.

**Prerequisite edges (listed separately; all `form: state`, all verbatim only in `premium_economy_upgrade_purchase_ed06e802` § "When the charge is fixed", confirmed by normalized substring search over all 78 docs):**

1. → ticket_ext_change_fee_posting: "The Premium Economy upgrade charge is fixed only after the latest standard exchange recorded on the ticket carries its change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a change fee." Connective "fixed only after", conditional strength ("whenever … owes") and state form unchanged. Basis: `change_fee_posting_dd5ba704` ("one itinerary-level change fee entry linked to that exchange entry"; "A fee worked out at zero is not recorded") + records (standard exchange e8b3cd9b, no linked entry).
2. → ticket_ext_bag_sequence_charge: "The Premium Economy upgrade charge on a segment is not fixed until every bag of that segment carrying a weight or size entry also carries its first, second or third bag charge." Basis: `bag_count_charge_posting_90ec0e43` ("each bag … that carries a weight or size entry but no first, second or third bag charge") + records (CR1047736).
3. → ticket_ext_bag_weight_charge: "Before the Premium Economy upgrade charge on a segment is fixed, the heaviest bag charged by count on that segment must carry its weight or size entry whenever it owes a weight or size charge." Basis: `bag_weight_size_charge_posting_68655b14` ("the heaviest bag carrying a first, second or third bag charge … when that bag carries no weight or size entry") + records (CR1047735, 72 lb).
None of the three sentences occurs in any other policy's document. `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` and `gate` are not rendered anywhere.

**Base ticket_corporate_agreement_benefits** (governs change fees and bags): `corporate_agreement_ticket_benefits_e2c03aca` carries the benefits, the active-status condition, the BE/award/companion exclusion and the no-stacking rule. Equal.

**Cross-product carriage (outside this skill's verdict range):** four factors (agreement relief, brand rate, corporate upgrade rate, trip-charge credit) and the corporate checked-bag allowance in the bag baseline rest on business-charter tier terms; the posting rate and the points rate read only agreement records the tools return (status, spend postings, points balance) and were fully settled blind. The ticket documents name "Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements" and the record kinds each tier reads, as the contract requires. The tier figures (`change_fee_waiver`, `annual_spend_threshold_usd`, `discount_eligible_fare_brands`, `fare_discount_percent_domestic`/`_international`, `booking_channels_eligible`, `corporate_free_checked_bags`) belong to the business corpus, which is not published. Whether that corpus carries them is not provable here.

## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the documents above traces to a source clause, compute binding, parameter or tool contract. All worked/boundary cases are marked hypothetical and are consistent. None reproduces task 1's opening world (e.g. the weight-counting example uses 52/53/51/55 lb and 58/46 lb, not 72/56).
- `weight_excess_rates_84dc7476` restates the weight/size charge selection to define "when the weight charge is the component recorded". This is the source's own condition of that factor (compute `w_weight_charge >= w_size_charge and w_weight_charge > 0`), not an addition.
- `bag_check_in_channel_rates_6801bdde` and `bag_count_list_charge_840f4929` both define the segment's check-in channel. The source puts the definition in the baseline and uses it as the factor's condition, so both homes are sourced.
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none. Each of the four tools is named only in its own policy's document.
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none.
- Added confirmations/reviews/notifications: none beyond the source's own "confirms and pays in person".

Additions / rewrites / omissions: none. The only observation is the hazard on the change-fee fare band wording, recorded above.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** All four extended policies (all 20 factor ladders in full, four self-sufficient computation documents with figures named), their base policies (all seven overwritten clauses — one change-fee, four bag, two paid-upgrade — present and marked retired, and no undeclared retirement), and the four tool contracts correspond losslessly at the level of entailment. All three prerequisite sentences stand verbatim, state form, only in the blocked hub. No previous revision.

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts; reported, not adjudicated):
- Undeclared partial override: base ticket_evt_bag_fees (not retired) prices a domestic first bag "when prepaid online or in the app" vs "when paid at the airport or through the call center", i.e. by the bag's own payment channel. ticket_ext_bag_sequence_charge prices it by "the segment's check-in channel" (online only when a segment bag charge was paid online and none at the airport). For a call-center posting on a segment whose other bags were prepaid online, the two give different fees (35 vs 40). The KB renders both, faithfully (`checked_baggage_charging_rules_fdcaf0de` § Sequence charges vs `bag_count_list_charge_840f4929` item 5). This task (short-haul international) does not reach the conflict.
- Tool contract vs seed: `task_tools.py` and the runtime schemas describe `bag_tag_number` as "CR followed by 6 digits", but the seeded tags are 7 digits (CR1047735, CR1047736, CR1039921). The KB follows the contract, and the gold argument is copied verbatim.

## dependency_form

- Ordering statements between problems: only the three verbatim prerequisite sentences in `premium_economy_upgrade_purchase_ed06e802` (whole-corpus scan for fixed/until/only after/before/then/prerequisite/wait). Every other hit is intra-policy ("unlocks it and then calls it"; "taken off … only after every rate … has acted on it").
- Depended-on documents (`change_fee_posting_dd5ba704`, `bag_count_charge_posting_90ec0e43`, `bag_weight_size_charge_posting_68655b14`, their computation and factor documents) never mention an upgrade or who waits on them.
- No state-form sentence is restated as an action or with the resolving tool/problem beside it. No route, checklist, dependency table, aggregated chain, or example/FAQ walks across problems. `premium_economy_trip_charges_7bda3fa4` lists "change, bag and upgrade charges" as the definition of trip charges (the source's own wording) and uses hypothetical figures. It does not state that any charge must be posted first.
- Titles are general ("Paid Upgrades into Premium Economy: Purchase Terms…", "Trip-Charge Credit on Premium Economy Upgrades for Corporate Bookings", "Checked-Bag Charges by Place in the Bag Count: Ledger Posting Reference", "Weight and Size Charges on Checked Bags: Ledger Posting Reference", "Change Fee Posting for Voluntary Exchanges"). None restates a customer request or mirrors this task's situation.
- Findability: the depended-on documents are reached with the sentences' and records' own words ("change fee entry", "standard exchange", "weight or size entry", "first, second or third bag charge", "heaviest bag").
- Factor documents: none names a typical tier, a mistake to avoid, the computation document or another factor by pointer. Uses of a defined quantity ("fare that bands the change fee/bag charge", "weight counted", "trip charges") are the source's term dependencies.
- Computation documents (`change_fee_by_origin_and_itinerary_bcda8477`, `bag_count_list_charge_840f4929`, `weight_size_list_charge_573a85de`, `premium_economy_upgrade_price_8c55cc7f`) contain no hint of modification. The baseline's "The weight counted is the recorded weight" is the source baseline sentence itself.

Blind hop marks: all three state-derived, none pre-solved.

**KB-EXPLICIT: PASS.**

## revision_2

- Round 1 had no RED, so none needs closing. The ticket corpus is unchanged (sha256 `ca2090e5…9116`), so the revision_1 source_to_kb, kb_to_source and dependency_form stand without change. Nothing regressed.
- Cross-product carriage item from revision_1 (the six Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements tier terms): now resolved at runtime. See runtime_context/…/1.md revision_2 for the doc-by-doc table. Every ticket factor document that rests on a business tier term names it in words the business corpus uses as its own column headers ("change fee waiver", "annual spend threshold", "discount-eligible fare brands", "negotiated discount … domestic and short-haul international", "eligible booking channels", "checked bags per direction"). The ticket-side findability requirement ("names that product by its official name and the kinds of records it reads") is therefore met in practice. Whether the business corpus is a faithful rendering of its own charter is outside this skill and was not judged.
- Dependency form: the business corpus names no ticket tool, contains no route or chain into the ticket upgrade problems, and says nothing about the upgrade charges (scoped scan: "trip-charge" 0 hits; "upgrade" hits only in company-points award and status-award documents). Its note that tickets booked under an agreement "receive the change fee waiver and the corporate checked bag allowance that the Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand rules apply from the tier's figures" is a benefit statement, not a cross-problem ordering.
- Observation carried to the business auditor and the policy side: the business "booked under the agreement" test (eligible channel + tour code + traveler on the active roster on the booking date) is framed differently from the ticket rules' "agreement named on the ticket and active". The task 1 world has an active agreement with no roster entries. In this world the difference changes no scored number (tier waiver no; corporate bag allowance 0).
